title: Soldier’s Joy (three-finger rolls)
short: Traditional (Scottish, then American) · D 4/4 · play it with every note lit.

blocks.html: Soldier’s Joy again, now in bluegrass style. You stay in open G tuning and play in D, with the D shape (0 2 3 4) and the A shape (a barre at the 2nd fret) under the left hand. The A part is an alternating-thumb roll with the thumb on the melody; the B part moves to the top strings, with pull-offs for the quick notes. Compare it with our clawhammer version in open D tuning: same tune, two ways.

blocks.name: music-player
blocks.cap: Play it: the score scrolls, the keys or strings light up as each note sounds.

blocks.html: The piece: Reel or country dance, printed in Britain from the late 1700s; an old-time standard in the American South

sources.name: Melody checked against “The Soldier’s Joy; or, Milanese Contre Dance” in Köhler’s Violin Repository, vol. 2 (Edinburgh, 1885), as transcribed in ABC by John Chambers at MIT (trillian.mit.edu); the book is on archive.org. Played an octave lower, starting on the downbeat. The note on every beat matches that version (on the beat or an eighth after it); between the beats we keep many of the tune’s notes and fill the rest with roll notes.
